blocks.content: In the above example, we have created an object named student of the child class. We have then used this object to access the public (name), protected (marks), and private (id) variables of Person.
However, when we run this code, we will get an error
This is because during public inheritance, the child class inherits variables from the parent class the way they were originally defined. Meaning

items: public variable name will be inherited as public in Student
protected variable marks will be inherited as protected, and
private variable id will be inherited as private.

blocks.content: And because of the accessibility (shown in the following table), we get an error.
We have already discussed how to access the private and protected variables from outside:

items: private variables - use public getter and setter functions
protected variables - access inside the subclass or use public getter and setter functions

blocks.content: We highly recommend you use both of this process and try to solve the issue in the above example.
